rows.Clause / Topic: Employer free-issue reinforcement steel delay - primary TIA clause
rows.Location: Clause 4.20 / Appendix advance payment steel supply / Clause 8.4 / Clause 20.1
rows.Plain English Meaning: Employer-supplied or client supplied reinforcement steel is tied to the approved programme and advance-payment arrangement. Late, short, or unusable free-issue steel can support a Delay TIA only when the Contractor proves timely requisition, readiness to use the steel, and critical path impact.
rows.Research the Lines: Priority keywords: steel, reinforcement, RFT, free issue, employer supplied, client supplied, material shortage, approved programme, requisition, delivery notes, stock records, activity impacts, critical path, TIA, EOT. This should rank first for steel shortage events. The Contractor position is strongest where the affected activity was ready, predecessors were complete, and the delay window is measured from stock-out/need date to usable recovery.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Shared - Contractor has leverage on time if records prove readiness and criticality; Employer has leverage if requisitions, readiness, or critical path are weak.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Immediate notice under Clause 20.1 and monthly claim account required. State activity ID, required steel date, requested quantity, delivered quantity, shortage, affected programme update, and intended TIA fragnet.
rows.Money Impact: Potential prolongation, disruption, and steel/concrete price adjustment only if non-Contractor delay and no uncompensable concurrency are proven.
rows.Schedule Impact: Strong EOT candidate if the stock-out delays a critical or longest-path activity, consumes float, or delays a contractual milestone after proper TIA insertion.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Approved baseline/update programme; steel requisitions; delivery notes; stock ledger; material inspection records; activity readiness proof; predecessor completion; photos; daily reports; CPM/TIA fragnet; concurrency review; notice and monthly claim updates.

rows.Plain English Meaning: The 25 percent advance includes a steel-supply component, with 70 percent as steel supplied by the Employer according to the approved programme.
rows.Research the Lines: This links free-issue steel to payment and programme administration. It does not by itself prove delay; it proves the source of supply and makes approved programme dates, requisitions, and delivery records central evidence.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify immediately when steel supply under the advance mechanism is late, short, or not usable against approved programme needs.
rows.Money Impact: Affects advance/payment reconciliation and may support prolongation or escalation only when delay responsibility is established.
rows.Schedule Impact: Supports causation for free-issue steel delay if the affected activity was ready and impacted the critical path.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Approved programme; advance-payment terms; steel delivery schedule; requisitions; receipts; delivery notes; shortage calculations; balance curve; correspondence requesting recovery commitments.

rows.Clause / Topic: Extension of Time entitlement and TIA proof
rows.Plain English Meaning: EOT is available only for qualifying Employer/Engineer risk events that delay completion or a contractual milestone and are claimed under the notice procedure.
rows.Research the Lines: Use this row for all Delay TIA conclusions. A valid event needs cause, effect, critical path/float impact, contemporaneous notice, and an update-impact/TIA calculation. Simple addition of delay days is not enough.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Shared - Contractor if critical path proof and notice are strong; Employer if delay is non-critical, concurrent, or unsupported.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Strict Clause 20.1 notice, particulars, updates, and monthly claim account. Missing or late notices create high time-bar risk.
rows.Money Impact: EOT protects from delay damages. Prolongation cost requires separate entitlement, causation, and concurrency proof.
rows.Schedule Impact: Primary schedule entitlement route for steel, RFI, IFC, access, variation, and suspension events.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Delay event register; notice register; impacted update; baseline/update schedules; fragnet logic; narrative; float path comparison; milestone impact; concurrency matrix; mitigation records.

rows.Clause / Topic: Clause 20.1 claim notice and time bar control
rows.Plain English Meaning: Failure to submit timely notice, particulars, and monthly claim updates can waive or severely weaken time and money claims.
rows.Research the Lines: This is the highest-risk defence against every otherwise valid claim. The Delay TIA engine should treat notice compliance as a gating issue, not an administrative afterthought.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer unless Contractor has complete notice trail
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Immediate protective notice; detailed particulars when available; repeat in monthly claim/variation account until resolved.
rows.Money Impact: Missed notice can defeat prolongation cost, disruption cost, variation recovery, and interest arguments.
rows.Schedule Impact: Missed notice can defeat or weaken EOT even where the technical schedule impact exists.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Notice letters; submission receipts; Engineer/Employer acknowledgements; monthly claim account; updated particulars; claim register; evidence index; responsible-party chronology.

rows.Clause / Topic: Delayed drawings, IFC revisions and Engineer instructions
rows.Plain English Meaning: Late drawings, delayed instructions, design revisions, or IFC conflicts may be Employer/Engineer risk when they stop approvals, procurement, inspection, or construction activities.
rows.Research the Lines: Use this for IFC conflict, revised structural drawings, missing information, delayed approvals, and RFI response delay. Entitlement depends on request date, required-by date, late response date, actual workface impact, and critical path effect.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notify once information is late or revision impact is known; identify affected activities and required response date.
rows.Money Impact: Potential prolongation or variation cost if the revision changes scope or causes non-concurrent delay.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT if late information delays critical design approval, procurement, inspection, or construction sequence.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: RFI/submittal logs; drawing register; transmittals; revision clouds; response dates; approval workflow; impacted activities; predecessor/successor logic; TIA fragnet; notice letters.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Late responses to RFIs, shop drawings, material approvals, or technical submittals can become a delay event where the response was required before work could proceed.
rows.Research the Lines: The key is not merely that an RFI was late; prove the answer was needed for a specific activity and that no reasonable alternate workfront avoided the impact.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Submit notice when response exceeds contractual/reasonable review period and affects planned work.
rows.Money Impact: Potential cost only if delay is Employer/Engineer risk and not concurrent with Contractor delay.
rows.Schedule Impact: Potential EOT where delayed response blocks critical or near-critical successor work.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: RFI register; submittal register; submission/reply dates; required-by date; affected activity ID; blocked workfront records; consultant comments; programme update; mitigation attempts.

rows.Clause / Topic: Programme requirements and critical path proof
rows.Plain English Meaning: The programme must be a proper CPM/P6 programme with logic, resources/cost/cash-flow where required, and regular updates. Delay claims depend on accepted programme logic.
rows.Research the Lines: The Delay TIA is only as strong as the schedule data. Float, longest path, predecessors, successors, calendars, progress status, and data date must be traceable.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer if programme is missing, unapproved, or logic is weak; Contractor if statused updates are complete.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Submit/revise programmes and narratives on time; include delay impacts in monthly reporting and claim accounts.
rows.Money Impact: Weak programme proof weakens prolongation and disruption claims.
rows.Schedule Impact: Critical path and EOT proof depends on accepted/current logic and statused update windows.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Baseline programme; update schedules; XER/PDF exports; calendars; logic report; longest-path report; float report; progress narrative; recovery plans; TIA insertion files.

rows.Plain English Meaning: Concurrent Employer and Contractor delays may allow time relief but can block or reduce money recovery for the concurrent period.
rows.Research the Lines: The concurrency matrix must split Employer delay, Contractor delay, neutral delay, and overlapping windows. Do not double count days. Separate entitlement to time from entitlement to cost.
rows.Who Holds Leverage: Employer on money; Contractor may retain time protection if critical Employer delay is proven.
rows.Notice / Time Bar: Notice still required for each Employer-risk event and each updated impact period.
rows.Money Impact: No or reduced prolongation cost during true concurrency unless contract/legal position supports apportionment.
rows.Schedule Impact: Possible EOT for net critical delay, subject to causation and notice.
rows.Practical Action / Evidence: Concurrency matrix; event windows; responsible party coding; critical path comparison; float consumption; contractor delay register; mitigation records; narrative explaining net impact.
